solution:
**Note:** The paper says 'collinear'; three lines through one point are concurrent, which is what is meant.

Three lines are concurrent (all passing through one point) if their determinant is zero: \(\begin{vmatrix}a&b&-c\\b&c&-a\\c&a&-b\end{vmatrix}=0\). Expanding gives \(a+b+c=0\) or \(a=b=c\). The general condition is \(a+b+c=0\). Common mistake: confusing concurrent lines with collinear lines.
